description:
Château des Forges was built in the 19th century by Anjou industrialist Germain Bouyonnet-Belize. It was later restored by an antique dealer and is positioned today as a "Slow Village" concept property — a deliberately contemporary, design-forward take on château life.

Today its 14 rooms combine antique furniture with contemporary comfort, all with balconies or terraces overlooking the valley, set in 6 hectares of parkland. The property is certified European Ecolabel.

The château's industrial-era origins, built by a local manufacturer rather than aristocratic or royal patrons, distinguish Château des Forges from the more traditionally noble-owned properties found elsewhere in the France collection.

The "Slow Village" branding and concept, embracing a relaxed and unstuffy approach to château hospitality, positions this property deliberately against the more formal, period-accurate luxury of many other French château-hotels.

The European Ecolabel certification gives Château des Forges a formally recognized environmental credential, reflecting its broader positioning around sustainability alongside its design sensibility.

The château's position on the outskirts of Angers gives guests staying at Château des Forges quick access to the city center and Château d'Angers, home to the Apocalypse Tapestry.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** On the outskirts of Angers, Maine-et-Loire, in Anjou.

**Rooms & rates:** 14 rooms from €63/night, all within the single 19th-century building, each with a balcony or terrace over the valley.

**On-site:** Outdoor pool with valley views, sun terrace, restaurant led by the creator of the "Green Punk Food" veggie brand, 6 hectares of parkland.

**Good to know:** The most design-forward, deliberately contemporary property in the France catalog — the "Slow Village" concept prioritizes a relaxed, unstuffy take on château life over period-accurate luxury; also one of the most affordable châteaux in the catalog and European Ecolabel certified.

**Combine with:** Angers city center and Château d'Angers, a short drive away.
